text:
sam: Quick q on KMS rotation strategy for envelope keys — do we want automatic rotation (scheduled rewrap) or lazy/manual rewrap on access? Trying to finalize rollout plan.

elaine: +1 we need to decide for both AWS/GCP/Azure. Automatic full rewrap could be expensive for a lot of objects. Lazy rewrap (on-read) minimizes work but prolongs exposure window.

mike: For Dedicated customers we promised deterministic rotation within N days. Auto rewrap may be required to meet SLA.

jia: Proposal: two-tier approach: 1) default = lazy rewrap on-read for blob stores, with background async rewriter for hot prefixes. 2) forced bulk rewrap for high-sensitivity tenants or on-request.

sam: That seems reasonable. How do we handle backwards compatibility in clients? We keep old KEK IDs in metadata, right?

elaine: Yes, store kek_version or kek_key_id with every wrapped DEK. Runtime picks correct KEK to decrypt. After rewrap, update metadata to point to new KEK. Keep old KEKs for 90 days minimum.

mike: Audit + rollback questions: We need audit logs for each rewrap operation (who/when/old_kek/new_kek/object). Ensure logs go to immutable store (s3/audit-project) and BigQuery for analysis.

sec-oncall: Also add RBAC: only rotation-service principal can call rewrap APIs. Limit to specific service accounts and require KMS key policy to allow rewrap. Add CloudTrail / Audit Logging filters to alert on unauthorized attempts.

infra-bot: deploybot: rotation-service rollout started in canary (tenants: test-1,test-2). Watch /metrics/rotation_success_rate

sam: Example commands for manual rewrap (AWS):
```bash
aws kms re-encrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://encrypted_dek.bin \
  --source-key-id alias/old-kek \
  --destination-key-id alias/new-kek \
  --output text > encrypted_dek_new.bin
```

jia: For GCP it's decrypt+encrypt step (no single re-encrypt API):
```bash
gcloud kms decrypt --ciphertext-file=enc_dek.bin --location=global --keyring=kr --key=old-kek --plaintext-file=plain_dek.bin
gcloud kms encrypt --plaintext-file=plain_dek.bin --location=global --keyring=kr --key=new-kek --ciphertext-file=enc_dek_new.bin
```

elaine: Migration strategy: 1) canary bulk rewrap small bucket during low-traffic window 2) enable lazy rewrap + background rewriter 3) after 30 days of zero failures, schedule full rewrap for remaining objects 4) retire old KEKs after retention period.

mike: Timings: aim for canary this week, background rewriter start next week, full rewrap in 30–45 days depending on perf.

sam: Failure modes? If rewrap fails mid-object we keep both ciphertexts and retry. If KMS key gets disabled, need emergency rollback: switch runtime to use previous KEK_id in metadata and halt rewriter.

sec-oncall: Add monitoring: rewrap_error_rate > 0.5% -> page sec-oncall. Also log latency regressions when using new KEKs (key policies, cross-region).

elaine: Action items: sam open RFC with detailed steps + per-cloud commands, mike update KMS key policies and audit log sinks, jia implement metadata versioning and background rewriter, sec-oncall write alert rules.

sam: I'll create the RFC and a runbook for rollback. Thanks.
